The cross-sectional information coefficient (IC) is the standard IC of factor research: each period, it is the Spearman correlation across many assets between their signal values at the end of the previous period and their returns over this period. The indicator owns one signal per asset: each input updates its asset's signal first, so the signals must not be updated elsewhere, such as by an algorithm helper that registered them. The indicator throws when it detects such an update. The signals can't be built from other indicators, as TimeSeriesInformationCoefficient explains. An asset's price is its input's value. Inputs whose end times fall in the same UTC period, at the inputs' resolution, form a period, so assets whose bars end at different local times, such as futures of different exchanges, share their daily periods. The indicator correlates a period as soon as every asset it tracks has an input for it. Otherwise, such as when an asset was delisted, it correlates the assets that have one when the next period starts. Each value has the end time of its period's last input, in the exchange time zone of the first asset given at construction. A period needs at least three assets with a signal value and a return. An asset with no input for a period pairs its last signal value with its return since then. Use Add and Remove to follow a changing cross-section, such as a universe's constituents.

To view the implementation of this indicator, see the LEAN GitHub repository.
